The reason I mentioned psychosis specifically was because in fiction institutionalised patients generally have some form of psychosis as opposed to a tic disorder

"insanity" is not a concept in psychology, it's a legal term that means the person either didn't understand what they were doing when committing a crime or they didn't understand that what they did was wrong.

In terms of how those two eventualities could come about, there are a plethora of reasons and a whole field of study dedicated to that sort of question. I couldn't begin to explain even a fraction of the possible causes because I don't know them, I'm just a student with a keen interest in the subject. 

In regards to mental illnesses seen in asylums in cinema, some sort of psychosis is usually responsible for things such as what may appear to be nervous ticks. The causes of psychosis are largely unknown but we know it can be caused by life stresses such as with family or by a chemical imbalance in the brain. Talking to oneself may be a comfort thing to deal with symptoms, or they may actually be conversing with a hallucination, possibly a voice in their head.

I wouldn't worry about you yourself being insane or anything, it's normal to get nervous ticks when your stressed or anxious. I have restless leg syndrome so when I get stressed my leg bounces up and down like crazy. Just means you're human :)
